'''Richard Earl Berendzen''' (September 6, 1938 – November 3, 2022) was an American scientist, [[professor]], and president of [[American University]], specializing in astronomy. His resignation in 1990 came following formal charges of making indecent phone calls to households in the Fairfax area over the course of several weeks that year. In 1992, he returned to American University as a full-time physics professor until his retirement in 2006.

==Early life==
Berendzen was born in [[Walters, Oklahoma]] on September 6, 1938. In 1942, he and his parents, Earl and June Berendzen, moved to [[Portland, Oregon]], where Berendzen developed [[rheumatic fever]] and [[asthma]] at a young age, which confined him to his room.<ref name="People1990"/><ref name="ALotofPain1990"/><ref name="AcademicStar1990"/>

In 1945, the family relocated to Dallas, Texas, where Earl managed a hardware store. Richard remained ill and bedridden for three more years, and began spending time stargazing on his lawn.{{R|"ALotofPain1990"|"People1990"}}

In 1946, Berendzen began attending school for the first time as a second grader.{{R|"ALotofPain1990"}} His mother's mental health began to deteriorate, and "she was wildly unpredictable. Labels like manic, paranoid, delusional, and psychotic came years later. Sometimes she would be furious for no apparent reason; then, in a snap, she could suddenly become incredibly loving, supportive, and fun.”{{Citation needed|date=November 2021}} Berendzen began experiencing sexual abuse in his home at this time.<ref name="comehere">{{cite book |last1=Berendzen |first1=Richard |title=Come Here: A Man Overcomes the Tragic Aftermath of Childhood Sexual Abuse |date=1993 |publisher=Villard Books |isbn=067941777X |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CGBHAAAAMAAJ |access-date=27 December 2020}}</ref>

==Education==

Berendzen attended [[Southern Methodist University]], where he pursued a physics degree. He transferred to [[MIT]] after his sophomore year{{R|"ALotofPain1990"}}<ref name="AUOutThere1986"/> and received a Bachelor of Science degree in 1961.{{R|"AcademicStar1990"}} He continued to Harvard as a graduate student, where he served as a teaching assistant for both [[William Liller]] and [[Carl Sagan]]. He graduated in 1967 with a master's degree and a joint PhD in astronomy and education.{{R|"ALotofPain1990"|"AUOutThere1986"}}<ref name="AUPresidents35Years"/>

==Career==

Berendzen joined the [[physics]] and [[astronomy]] faculty at [[Boston University]], and became the chair of the astronomy department in 1971.{{R|"AUPresidents35Years"}} In 1974, he was hired as the dean of the college of arts and sciences at [[American University]] in Washington, D.C.{{R|"ALotofPain1990"|"AUOutThere1986"|"AUPresidents35Years"}} American University appointed him as [[provost (education)|provost]] in 1976,{{R|"AcademicStar1990"}} and in 1980 he became the university's eleventh president.{{R|"ALotofPain1990"|"AUPresidents35Years"}}

During his 10-year tenure as president, Berendzen and his wife Gail averaged eleven Washington social functions every week, and the university's endowment tripled in size.{{R|"PowerfulIsDoes"|"People1990"}}

Berendzen secured a $5 million donation from Saudi businessman [[Adnan Khashoggi]] toward the Adnan Khashoggi Sports and Convocation Center, and named Kashoggi to the university's board of trustees.{{R|"PowerfulIsDoes"}} Khashoggi's donation, and the building's subsequent naming, elicited limited protests from some American University students and former faculty who were concerned about Khashoggi's role in the [[Iran-Contra affair]].<ref name="AUDefendsGift"/> Khashoggi was removed from the board in 1989 after facing charges of racketeering, fraud and obstruction of justice pertaining to his dealings in the Philippines.<ref name="AdnanSeizedSwiss"/>
<ref name="AdnanNameRemoved"/>

In addition to his responsibilities at American University, Berendzen chaired the commission on the Budget and Financial Priorities of the District of Columbia<ref name="WADecline" />{{When|date=November 2021}} and the American Council on Education's Committee on Foreign Student Policy.<ref name="ChairmanNCFSP" />{{When|date=November 2021}} He was also an original member of the [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry|Committee for the Scientific Investigation of Claims of the Paranormal]].<ref name="CSICop2001" />

[[File:Life Beyond Earth and the Mind of Man - Carl Sagan on Aliens NASA Film.webm|thumb|Berendzen at the "Life Beyond Earth and the Mind of Man" panel, November 1972]]

He served on the board of the [[Planetary Society]]<ref name="PlanetarySociety" /> and the advisory board for the National Center for the Survivors of Child Abuse.<ref name="UndoingDamage1993" /> He was a consultant to NASA,<ref name="NASAConsultant" /> served on NASA's Exploration Advisory Task Force,<ref name="NASAAdvisoryCouncil" /> and Selection Panel for the [[Teacher in Space Project]],<ref name="TeacherInSpace" /> served as director of NASA's Space Grant Consortium for Washington, D.C.,{{R|"PlanetarySociety"}} and testified about space and education before the [[United States Congress]].<ref name="SETI" />

Under the auspices of the New York Academy of Sciences and the American Astronomical Society, Berendzen organized and chaired a major international conference, titled "Education in and History of Modern Astronomy."<ref name="InternationalConference" /> He organized and chaired two other key conferences: "Life Beyond Earth and the Mind of Man" (at [[Boston University]]) in 1973 and "Space 2000" (at [[American University]]) in 1999.<ref name="LifeBeyondEarth" /><ref name="Space2000" /> Proceedings from the Boston University were included in ''Who's Out There?'', a 1975 television program narrated by [[Orson Welles]].<ref name="WhosOutThere" /><ref name="1975NASASearchFilm" />

==Resignation from American University==
In March 1990, daycare owner Susan Allen received a phone call from a man claiming to be a gynecologist and inquiring about her sexual habits. She reported the call to her husband, a Fairfax County law enforcement officer, and continued to engage with the caller for several weeks while police monitored the communication via call tracing and tape recordings. Allen described the calls as "filthy beyond your most horrible nightmares."{{R|"ALotofPain1990"}}<ref name="WashingtonPost"/>

Police traced the calls to American University and Berendzen's private phone line.{{R|"WashingtonPost"}} Among other things, Berendzen asked those he called whether they had sex with children, claimed he kept a 4-year-old sex slave in his basement, and made repeated references to child pornography and purchasing child sex slaves at auction.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bauers |first1=Sandy |title=Obscene Phone Calls And Bitter Allegations Richard Berendzen's Appearance Left Many In The Audience With Mixed Feelings |url=http://articles.philly.com/1994-05-15/living/25829613_1_childhood-sexual-abuse-richard-berendzen-child-pornography |website=Philly.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151223051606/http://articles.philly.com/1994-05-15/living/25829613_1_childhood-sexual-abuse-richard-berendzen-child-pornography |archive-date=2015-12-23 }}</ref> On April 7, the board of trustees confronted Berendzen, who resigned on April 8. He was admitted to Johns Hopkins, where he was treated with several therapies addressing his childhood abuse.<ref name="PopeRecoveredMemories"/><ref name="FalseMemorySyndrome"/> On April 10, Berendzen issued a public statement citing "exhaustion" as the reason behind his decision to step down.{{R|"People1990"|"AcademicStar1990"}}<ref name="BerendzenCharged" />

===Aftermath===
Berendzen was charged with two misdemeanor counts of making indecent calls.{{R|"BerendzenCharged"}} He pleaded guilty to both, and his jail time was suspended on the condition that he continue receiving psychiatric treatment for the next year.<ref name=apnewsguilty>{{cite web |last1=Womack |first1=Anita |title=Former American University President Pleads Guilty to Making Obscene Calls |url=https://apnews.com/article/333a7bcf118c10fa90252913d82ecee3 |website=AP News |publisher=Associated Press |access-date=27 December 2020 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20201227224905/https://apnews.com/article/333a7bcf118c10fa90252913d82ecee3 |archive-date=27 December 2020}}</ref><ref name="AUPact"/> Once the case became public, more than two dozen other daycare providers in the Fairfax area reported to police that they had also received obscene calls.{{R|"People1990"}}

In the summer of 1990, Allen filed an $11 million lawsuit against Berendzen and American University.<ref name="AUBerendzenSued"/> The case was settled for an undisclosed sum.<ref name="PrimalScream"/>

In 1992, Berendzen returned to American University as a full-time physics professor, and served in that role until he retired in August 2006.{{R|"AUPact"}}<ref name="returnstoAU">{{cite web |last1=Baer |first1=Susan |title=Richard Berendzen returns to American University One-time president to teach astronomy |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/1991/12/25/richard-berendzen-returns-to-american-university-one-time-president-to-teach-astronomy/ |publisher=Baltimore Sun |access-date=27 December 2020 |date=25 December 1991}}</ref>

==Accomplishments==
Berendzen received [[honorary doctorate]] degrees from Seton Hall University<ref name="Steton" /> and the University of Columbo<ref name="Columbo" /> in 1985, and from the University of Maryland in 1990.<ref name="umdhonorary">{{cite web |title=University of Maryland Honorary Degree Search |url=https://www.usmd.edu/regents/honorarydegrees/ |website=University System of Maryland |access-date=28 December 2020 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20201228144507/https://www.usmd.edu/regents/honorarydegrees/ |archive-date=28 December 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Berendzen met his first wife, Barbara Edwards, at [[Woodrow Wilson High School (Dallas)|Woodrow Wilson High School]]. Their first daughter, Deborah, was born during Berendzen's first year at SMU.{{R|"ALotofPain1990"}} In 1960, while Berendzen was at MIT, Barbara returned to Dallas with Deborah, and the couple divorced.{{R|"AUOutThere1986"|"ALotofPain1990"}}

Berendzen married Gail Edgar, whom he met at Harvard, in 1964,{{R|"ALotofPain1990"}} and the couple had a daughter named Natasha.{{R|"Kirkus"}}

Berendzen died of a respiratory ailment at his [[Arlington, Virginia]], home on November 3, 2022. He was 84.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Harrison |title=Richard Berendzen, AU president who resigned in scandal, dies at 84 |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/obituaries/2023/03/27/richard-berendzen-american-university-dead/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=March 27, 2023}}</ref>
